normalizing_flow.summary: A conditional RealNVP flow learns the exact density of the bar's feature row under each outcome; Bayes' rule turns the densities into P(up).
normalizing_flow.implementationNote: Bridge: exact log p(row | outcome) from a class-conditional RealNVP (ActNorm, fixed permutations, affine couplings), Bayes' rule with the training priors, one temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: it models the current feature row, not generated prices; rows are clipped at 6 standard deviations. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

neural_ode_generator.summary: A continuous normalizing flow (FFJORD): a neural ODE carries the feature row to a Gaussian, and the integrated Jacobian trace gives its exact density under each outcome.
neural_ode_generator.implementationNote: Bridge: exact log p(row | outcome) from a class-conditional FFJORD flow (torchdiffeq RK4, exact trace when scoring, Hutchinson in training, kinetic penalty), Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: continuous time matters only across session gaps; bars inside a session are evenly spaced. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths. The slowest scorer here.

pixel_autoregressive.summary: The feature row is read as a one-dimensional image of quantile tokens; a class-conditional PixelCNN (or PixelRNN) gives its exact likelihood column by column.
pixel_autoregressive.implementationNote: Bridge: exact log p(tokens | outcome) = sum of log p(token_i | earlier tokens, outcome) over train-quantile tokens of the row, from gated causal convolutions (PixelCNN) or a GRU (PixelRNN); Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: the column order is arbitrary, so the convolution's locality prior is too. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

generative_pretrained_transformer.summary: A decoder-only transformer reads an outcome token then the row's quantile tokens and predicts each next token; the exact likelihood under each outcome feeds Bayes' rule.

diffusion_model.summary: A class-conditional DDPM learns to remove noise from the bar's feature row; the outcome whose model denoises the row best is the likely one (the diffusion classifier).
diffusion_model.implementationNote: Bridge: diffusion classifier - score_k is minus the mean epsilon-prediction error of the outcome-k DDPM (cosine schedule) on one fixed grid of (step, noise) draws; Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled. Expect: class-conditional density of the current row plus Bayes' rule, not future paths; the denoising error is an ELBO surrogate calibrated on validation.

perceptual_loss_generator.summary: A diffusion model trained with a perceptual loss: denoised rows are compared in the feature space of a frozen autoencoder fitted first on the training rows; the combined error ranks the outcomes.
perceptual_loss_generator.implementationNote: Bridge: clean-row DDPM whose loss adds the distance in a FROZEN autoencoder's hidden layers (fitted first on the training rows); score_k is minus that error on a fixed noise grid; Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: no VGG exists for market rows; the perceptual space is learned. Expect: class-conditional density of the current row plus Bayes' rule, not future paths; the denoising error is an ELBO surrogate calibrated on validation.

energy_based_model.summary: A joint energy model (JEM): one network scores every outcome's energy for the row, trained on the labels and, with Langevin-sampled negatives, as a density of the rows themselves.
energy_based_model.implementationNote: Bridge: JEM - f(x) gives the joint energy of (row, outcome); the shared normaliser cancels, so P(k | row) is softmax(f), with one validation temperature. Training: cross-entropy plus the likelihood term with SGLD negatives from a replay buffer; unlabelled training rows count as real data. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled for use. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

bayesian_generator.summary: Per outcome, a Gaussian mixture with a Dirichlet-process prior over its latent components is fitted by variational Bayes on the whitened rows; the prior decides how many components survive.
bayesian_generator.implementationNote: Bridge: log p(row | outcome) of a variational-Bayes Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture per outcome on whitened rows, Bayes' rule with training priors, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: its VAE reading is the VAE entry and its Bayesian-weights reading the Bayesian neural hybrid; this is the shallow Bayesian generator. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

deep_boltzmann_machine.summary: A two-hidden-layer Gaussian-Bernoulli deep Boltzmann machine whose visible layer holds the row and the outcome; the outcome with the lower free energy is the likely one.
deep_boltzmann_machine.implementationNote: Bridge: joint DBM over (row, one-hot outcome): greedy CD-1 pretraining, then mean-field data statistics and persistent Gibbs chains; score_k is the mean-field lower bound on log p~(row, k), the partition function cancels; validation temperature. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled for use; the bound is not exact. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

masked_autoencoder_density.summary: A class-conditional masked autoencoder hides most of the row's tokens and reconstructs them from the rest; how well each outcome's model fills the gaps ranks the outcomes. MADE masks give an exact likelihood instead.
masked_autoencoder_density.implementationNote: Bridge: score_k is minus the masked Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the hidden tokens (learned per-column variance) averaged over fixed masks, or the exact MADE likelihood with mask_style autoregressive_made; Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: tokens are groups of feature columns; random masks give a pseudo-likelihood. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.
